text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I pulled flash-attn@main + vLLM recent xformers compat PR and ran a short smoke on prod-sim GPU pool. seeing a perf dip for long sequences when paged-attn is enabled.

maria: baseline (flash-attn pinned at v1.2.0, no xformers patches) vs upstream combo:
```
seq=2048, batch=2, tokens/s: baseline=5200, upstream=4400 (-15%)
seq=4096, batch=1, tokens/s: baseline=2100, upstream=1600 (-24%)
latency p95: baseline=120ms -> upstream=160ms
```

drew: ouch. did you toggle KV cache behavior? could be cache miss pattern with paged layout.

maria: good call. I ran with KV disabled and numbers recovered ~within 5% of baseline. so it looks tied to KV + new attention changes.

ravi: @maria can you paste the exact commit SHAs for flash-attn and vllm/xformers? want to bisect.

maria: flash-attn: `a3f7d9c` (main, last week). vllm: PR #238 (uses xformers patch that changes block size heuristics). link: https://github.com/vllm/vllm/pull/238

sophie: fyi vendor-driver had a minor cuda patch this week too (vendorA-driver 525.60 -> 525.73). could be kernel fallback triggering.

drew: hypothesis: new xformers patch changes attention tiling; for small batches it increases kernel launches and prevents fused kernel from hitting fast path -> KV gets more fragmented -> more memory thrash.

tim: can we repro with synthetic microbench to isolate kernel selection? i can run a sweep across batch, seq, kv-enabled toggles.

maria: yes — I already threw together a microbench script (quick, unoptimized). results attached below.
```bash
# run: python perf_microbench.py --model gpt2 --seq 4096 --batch 1 --kv on/off
# summary
kv:on  tokens/s=1600  p95=158ms
kv:off tokens/s=2050  p95=123ms
```

ravi: thanks. next step: bisect flash-attn commit range to see when kernel selection change happened. likely candidate: the paging+fusion refactor from two weeks ago.

sophie: I can spin a dedicated canary on dedicated-gpu-3 to run the bisect overnight. will also test vendorA driver 525.60 rollback to check for driver interactions.

ci-bot: CI: nightly perf job failed threshold: p95 latency increased by 18% for seq=4096 on canary. Job: nightly/perf-attn-4096 (see logs).

maria: noted. I also saw an odd nvprof-ish log entry where a kernel fell back to `gemm_fallback_kernel` around large KV offsets. attaching stack snippet in case it's useful.

maria: ```
[2026-03-14 03:12:22] launch kernel: fused_attn_forward_tile_v2 -> fallback to generic gemm_fallback_kernel (tile 7)
[2026-03-14 03:12:22] mem_copy: async wait 2.3ms
```

drew: that fallback explains the latency jump. need to check kernel selection heuristics: tile size, vector width, and rvv path in flash-attn.

tim: action items I can take tomorrow:
- run bisect on flash-attn commits to identify regression commit
- reproduce with and without xformers patches
- test driver rollback on canary
- gather kernel launch counts and occupancy reports

ravi: i'll review the vllm PR to see if the requested change to blocksize heuristics is optional. if so we can flip it behind a flag for now.

maria: also let's add a quick guard in our runtime: if paged-attention + KV enabled + seq>2048, force `fused_kernel` compatibility mode (cheap toggle) until upstream is stable. will send a draft patch.

sophie: +1 for guard. reduces blast radius.

maria: draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/reimpl/pull/456 (WIP) — adds runtime flag `force_fused_attn_compat`.

drew: one more ask: can we add a perf regression test in CI that exercises seq 4096, kv on, paged-attn on so we catch this earlier?

ci-bot: Issue created: #789 perf-regression-detect-4096-kv (assigned to eng-runtime).

maria: will follow up with bisect results tomorrow. thanks all for quick triage. :white_check_mark:

tim: thanks — if anyone wants cluster access for experiments ping me and i'll open a slot on dedicated-gpu-3.

sophie: leaving notes in the runbook under eng-runtime/attn-upstream for triage steps and where to find traces.

maria: last: recording the root cause hypothesis for posterity — interaction between xformers tiling heuristics and KV page offsets causing kernel fallback -> perf regression. need confirmation via bisect and driver matrix.

ravi: copy. will coordinate with vendorA on driver fallbacks if we can reproduce deterministically.

maria: thread closed for now; will reopen if bisect points elsewhere.
